spec: Build an image-gallery backend. Images are stored in S3 and organised into albums whose metadata lives in DynamoDB. Users can create albums, upload images to an album via presigned URLs, list images in an album, and delete images or whole albums.

complexity.rationale: Couples albums and image metadata with object storage and a presigned upload flow.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint listing images in an album
DELETE endpoints for images and albums

plan.summary: A FastAPI JSON backend for an image gallery. Albums are metadata records in DynamoDB; image binaries live in an S3 bucket while their metadata lives in a second DynamoDB table keyed by album. Clients create albums, request short-lived presigned S3 PUT URLs to upload image bytes directly to S3, confirm the upload so metadata is finalised, list images (with presigned GET URLs for viewing), and delete individual images or whole albums (which cascades to the album's S3 objects and image records). The service runs as a standalone process and calls S3 and DynamoDB directly with boto3; no asynchronous or event-driven cloud execution is required, so no Lambda, SQS or API Gateway is planned.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe reporting that the service can reach its S3 bucket and DynamoDB tables.
Create a new album; writes an album metadata item (id, title, description) to the albums DynamoDB table.
List all albums with basic metadata and image counts (paginated scan of the albums table).
Fetch a single album's metadata; 404 if the album does not exist.
Update mutable album metadata such as title or description.
Delete an album, all of its image metadata items, and all of its objects under the album prefix in the S3 bucket.
Register a pending image and return a presigned S3 PUT URL (plus the S3 key and expiry) the client uses to upload the bytes directly to S3.
Confirm an upload finished: HEAD the S3 object, record size/content-type, and flip the image status from pending to available.
List image metadata for an album (DynamoDB query on the album partition key), each entry including a presigned GET URL for viewing.
Fetch a single image's metadata together with a presigned GET download URL.
Delete one image: remove the S3 object and its DynamoDB metadata item, decrementing the album's image count.

aws_resources.name: image-gallery-media
aws_resources.justification: Stores the image binaries; the backend generates presigned PUT/GET URLs against this bucket and deletes objects when images or albums are removed. CORS is configured so browser clients can PUT directly to the presigned URL.

aws_resources.name: albums
aws_resources.justification: Holds album metadata (album_id partition key) created, read, updated and deleted by the /albums endpoints.

aws_resources.name: images
aws_resources.justification: Holds per-image metadata with album_id partition key and image_id sort key so listing images in an album is a single Query and cascade delete of an album can enumerate its images.

aws_resources.name: image-gallery-app-policy
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy (and an access identity for the service) granting exactly the s3:PutObject/GetObject/DeleteObject/ListBucket on the media bucket and dynamodb Get/Put/Update/Delete/Query/Scan on the two tables that the backend calls.

aws_resources.name: /image-gallery/app-logs
aws_resources.justification: Log group the backend ships its structured application and S3/DynamoDB error logs to for operational visibility.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 6 files — FastAPI image-gallery backend split into a thin HTTP layer (app.py) and an AWS data-access layer (storage.py). storage.py exposes DynamoS3GalleryRepository, which lazily builds boto3 S3/DynamoDB handles honouring AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION (default us-east-1) and reads S3_BUCKET/ALBUMS_TABLE/IMAGES_TABLE/PRESIGN_EXPIRES_SECONDS from the environment with plan-matching defaults. It implements album CRUD (with paginated scan and opaque base64 tokens), presigned PUT registration, upload completion via head_object, image listing/query with presigned GET URLs, per-image delete, and cascading album delete (query image items + list_objects_v2 prefix sweep, batched delete_objects and batch_writer deletes). Domain exceptions (AlbumNotFound, ImageNotFound, ObjectNotUploaded) are mapped to 404/404/409 through FastAPI exception handlers; the repository is injected as a dependency so tests can override it. tests/test_app.py covers every endpoint with an in-memory FakeRepository plus storage unit tests using boto3 stubs and helper/env assertions — no network or LocalStack needed. Root conftest.py fixes sys.path; requirements.txt lists only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic; README documents configuration, run steps and the three-step upload flow. No hardcoded secrets, no debug literals, dev server binds 127.0.0.1 by default.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the image-gallery backend, scoped strictly to the plan's aws_resources: an S3 media bucket (KMS SSE with bucket keys, versioning, full public-access block, TLS-only bucket policy, lifecycle rules with multipart abort, CORS for browser presigned PUT/GET, and access logging into a dedicated hardened log bucket), two DynamoDB tables (albums keyed by album_id; images keyed by album_id + image_id) with point-in-time recovery and KMS SSE, a CloudWatch Logs group /image-gallery/app-logs with 365-day retention and KMS encryption, and an IAM role plus image-gallery-app-policy granting only the exact S3 object/list, DynamoDB item/query/scan, log-write and KMS envelope-encryption actions on those specific ARNs. A rotated customer-managed KMS key with an explicit, non-wildcard key policy (account admin statements plus a scoped CloudWatch Logs service statement) satisfies encryption checks. Files: versions.tf (hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 pin), variables.tf (defaults matching plan resource names), main.tf (provider default_tags with project/managed-by, all resources), outputs.tf. No Lambda, SQS, SNS or API Gateway since the plan requires none; two Checkov skips with reasons cover S3 event notifications and cross-region replication, which this single-region synchronous design does not use.
